patients.label: 25-year-old woman with Crohn disease and a recurrent right psoas abscess initially attributed to perforated appendicitis
attribution_limitations: Crohn disease duration is stated as an 11-year history in the abstract and a 10-year history in the case presentation; both are kept review-only and neither is used in labels or summaries.

The introduction presents this case as having a psoas-enteric fistula, while the case narrative records only concern for a retrocecal fistula and for a recurrent fistula and the second laparoscopy found no obvious cause for the recurrent abscess; the fistula is kept review-only and no fistula is recorded as confirmed.

The abstract mentions two drainages before and three after ileocecectomy; the narrative describes drains in separate visits and states only a third IR drain placed at a separate hospital, so total drain counts are not reconciled.

The outpatient presentation and the emergency room visit two weeks earlier, and the later presentation for re-evaluation nine days after the first drain, are not identified as the same or different encounters, so they are kept as separate events without an ordering link between the outpatient presentation and the re-evaluation.
The authors attribute the abscess recurrence to possible epithelialization of the abscess cavity; this is a hedged cause and is not recorded as a fact.

The sentence listing pain extending to the back, fever and increased CRP does not state when these were present; the time phrase at initial presentation may apply only to the abdominal pain and abscess.
